Victims of hereditary disorders may have inspired tales of vampires.
Throughout the centuries, myths have been used to explain the bizarre events and behaviors. Due to a lack of medical knowledge and general fear of the unknown, communities would target and shun people who were different. It must have been a frightening time for people who knew little about human diseases. One such myth was the belief in vampires who would suck human blood and preferred to live in darkness. In fact, these were often people who were suffering from a rare hereditary illness called porphyria.

Porphyria is the Greek word for “purple”. A major symptom of the disease was that a victim's urine turned dark blue or purple in color because their body was struggling to produce heme, an essential component of red blood. There were other symptoms of the disease including extreme sensitivity to sunlight, sores and scars, excessive hair growth and tightening of skin around lips and gums. Changes to the mouth may have given sufferers a “vampire appearance”.

Tragically, a common misconception was that when an individual ingested a healthy person's blood, they were replenishing the victim's own blood supply. Fear, ignorance of the disease and general intolerance often led to the persecution of many people. Victims of the disease must have felt isolated and misunderstood.
While sufferers lived as recluses, medical scientists were investigating the cause of the bizarre symptoms. They discovered that after they gave patients regular heme injections, they were seeing significant results. People who previously suffered from this condition were now living ‘normal' lives instead of being condemned by their communities.
Myths explain why an event occurs.

You use modals when you want to express possibility and certainty.

You use may, might and could to express possibility in the past and in the future.
*Might suggests that something is less possible than may

  • might / might not + infinitive
  • could / could not + infinitive
  • may / may not + infinitive

Example:

Fear and ignorance could have been the reason for the persecution of victims.
Communities may have thought that sufferers were dangerous.

Expressing Certainty

You use must to express that something is necessarily true.

Example:

She must have felt like he didn't care about her.
Victims of the disease must have felt isolated and misunderstood.
You use the Simple Past tense to talk about events that are finished. You use the Past Continuous to talk about events or an action that was happening at a time in the past.

Simple Past tense verbs can be regular or irregular.

Regular verbs end in -ed or -ied.

Irregular verbs change in different ways.

For questions in the past, you use the auxiliary did followed by the verb in the base form, like Did you ask ... ?

Did is the past form of to do.

For Past Continuous, we add was/were + verb“ing” to verbs.
Some verbs need a change to the last letter to add “ing”.
